### Commit accepted tasks and review and merge controller runs

```yaml
id: T-564a522f-39e1-421c-97fb-6a35a49f3cc9
priority: 101
status: Ready
parent_pending_ids: ["P-f15fdc5c-4e37-451d-9d1b-a261e7bd199a"]
processing_run_id: PR-2dbc0122-fcfa-433f-a1a9-d05fa579d8f6
root_task_id: T-564a522f-39e1-421c-97fb-6a35a49f3cc9
related_task_id: null
relation: main
depends_on: []
intake_batch_ids: ["IB-83431b00-0b18-4915-9152-d9162d75294c"]
```

Goal:
- Commit accepted tasks through the normal implementation operations and deliver reviewed controller runs according to the agreed local Git defaults.

Current behavior:
- The completed Implement All run WR-e22aaaa6-321f-4acb-92f9-4d0302a8b47d ended with local changes. Local commit 1723950 was created afterward by a separate instruction.
- [Workflow state](../common/scripts/workflow-state.py) validates checks and acceptance in `complete`, copies optional commit references into the terminal outcome, and starts local delivery from `finish` only for a pre-existing local merge order.
- [Workspace tools](../common/scripts/run-workspaces.py) default the source base to remote `develop`. Existing local delivery binds the authorized base and expects the merge target to be checked out in the canonical queue worktree. The invocation worktree can have a different checked-out local branch.
- [Repository instructions](../../AGENTS.md) require explicit commit authorization. [Operation templates](../templates/operations.json) and [workspace guidance](../common/references/run-workspaces.md) currently offer a separate local-result handoff.

Touch:
- Shared task completion and recovery, controller launch and local delivery, exact Git review identity, canonical queue routing, authored operation templates, repository rules, generated package resources and relevant fixture suites.
- Reuse the owned task validation, decision/review and local Git delivery guards. Capture the launch worktree branch and commit before provisioning. Verify checked-out identity and current source/target at delivery. Preserve the launch ancestry and unrelated edits.
- Keep exact task commit receipts in terminal outcomes. Record review corrections as scoped fix commits when findings require source changes. Preserve accepted task commits and current required checks.
- Bind late Work Through Next merge authorization to the reviewed run and recorded start branch. Keep previously recorded orders and terminal records intact. Preserve existing explicitly ordered PR/merge flows and require explicit authorization for remote publication.

Validation:
- Strategy: reproduce missing commit, unsafe retry and wrong-target behavior in disposable Git repositories before fixes. Exercise normal skill and controller entry points with current review/check evidence.
- Run reference synchronization, strict repository validation, the Python and Node suites, installer inventory and a general installer dry run, and Git diff checks.

Acceptance:
- Implement Next commits one accepted task on the checked-out branch in the selected worktree after current checks and review. Each controller commits every task accepted during the run exactly once, including required dependencies.
- The verified task commit binds the exact branch, prior head and owned change set. Failed application and lost acknowledgement preserve recoverable progress, and retries reuse the original commit. Unrelated staged, unstaged and untracked content survives. Ambiguous overlap stops before a Git write.
- Implement All and Work Through Next preserve one run worktree and perform full local review, actual fixes when required and repeat review against the current committed head and recorded start branch.
- Implement All merges after a clean current review. Work Through Next reaches a review-ready branch by default and supports explicit merge authorization at launch or after review for the same run. Both merge paths target the exact recorded launch branch, including a linked worktree with local commits. Drift, conflicts or dirty overlap preserve recoverable work and prevent a wrong-branch merge.
- Existing recorded delivery orders and terminal outcomes retain provenance. Explicit full-cycle PR delivery preserves the requested remote scope. Core commit and local delivery defaults cause zero remote writes.
- Authored repository rules and installed Implement Next, Work Through Next and Implement All packages agree on scoped commit and local delivery defaults. The blanket extra-authorization requirement for task commits is retired while remote publication continues to require explicit authorization.
